## Review — PR #11322 · substance **ACCEPT** · ⛔ flip deferred (CI still converging)

### Disclosure discipline — checked first, before anything else

Clause 4 was the one most likely to be violated by a well-meaning implementation, so I checked it before reading for correctness, and I checked the **diff**, not just the body.

- **PR body**: describes what is asserted and why. The structural facts it cites (the baseline names no grant for this object; no ADR-0103 `managedBy` bucket while seven siblings declare one; neither column carries `readonly` while `id` does) are already published on this card. No seeding steps, no request shapes, no values, no endpoint recipe. ✅
- **The committed file**: the decisive question was whether it was authored as a *pin* or as the *harness*. It is a pin. The measurement's second posture — the one where an app-authored wildcard grant is union-merged onto the baseline and **both** non-admin personas get through — is the sensitive half, because it is the half that shows how to open the hole. **It is absent from this diff.** It stayed in QA #10663 where the card put it. ✅
- Commit message and comments: clean. ✅

This comment observes the same discipline: properties only, no recipe.

### The four binding clauses, against the diff

| clause | verdict |
|---|---|
| `code` **and** `status` (ADR-0112) | ✅ both asserted, never status alone |
| platform-admin contrast control, same row + same columns | ✅ present, and load-bearing |
| read-back asserted, not the response | ✅ every case re-reads under a system context, above every access layer |
| disclosure discipline | ✅ as above |

Three things the implementation got right that I did not ask for, and that are the difference between a pin and a decoration:

1. **The envelope reader handles both spellings.** The data surface answers a denial flat while other surfaces nest it under `error`. A pin that knew only one spelling would read a genuine refusal as "no code" — failing for the wrong reason, or worse, passing vacuously if the assertion were written loosely. Reading both is what makes the `code` assertion mean what it says.

2. **The contrast control has its own control.** The admin case asserts that the values it writes actually differ from the seeded ones before writing them. Without that, the control itself could pass vacuously — a control that writes what is already there proves nothing about reaching the endpoint. Guarding the guard is the exact discipline this clause exists to enforce, applied one level deeper than the clause demanded.

3. **The control runs last, deliberately.** It is the only case that changes the row, so every refusal case above it ran against the seeded state, and it still addresses the same row and columns they did. Ordering here is not cosmetic: it is what makes "same row, same columns" true rather than merely claimed.

Also unprompted and correct: the **seed control as its own named case**, so a fixture that landed differently fails naming itself instead of letting a later refusal read as a pass; and the **null write covered separately from the value write**, on the stated reasoning that clearing a column is the cheaper way to disarm a re-check that reads it. That is a threat-model judgement, not coverage padding.

### Ablation

Predicted before running, both directions, and it caught the trap this repo has been bitten by: the mutation was confirmed **on disk and in the built artifact the suite actually consumes**, because this suite resolves that package from `dist` — an unrebuilt ablation would have reported a false green and "proved" the pin worked when nothing had changed under it. Refusal cases red, contrast control green, restore byte-identical, rebuilt, marker-clean, re-verified to a real green. Predicted direction and observed direction match.

### Scope held

⛔ The un-ruled posture question — whether this object should be engine-owned, or these columns readonly / system-managed — is **not decided**, and the pin is written to survive either outcome. That was the constraint, and it holds.

### ⛔ Why this is not a flip yet

CI on `fb0c37d6`: **32 checks, zero failures**, but several still running — `Test Core (1/6)`, three Dogfood gates, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, and three Type Check lanes. Green is read **by job name** when the run finishes, never off an aggregator and never early. This shift already corrected one ACCEPT that called CI green minutes before a real failure landed.

One item to close at flip time: the PR declares a narrowing — `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` was not run locally (it needs the whole workspace built), with the package's own `typecheck` run to a real green instead. **Declared, not silently skipped**, which is the right way to handle it — and CI's `Type Check · debt ledger` runs the family regardless, so that job passing is what discharges it.

**Clause-②: no** — confirmed against the landed diff. One new test file, no behaviour change, nothing in the accept/reject set moves. `skip-changeset` is correct: one test file in a private package that publishes nothing.

## Addendum — two measured facts from the implementation round that outlive this PR

Recording these on the card because they bear on the **un-ruled posture question** this pin was deliberately built to survive, and they would otherwise live only in an agent report.

### 1. ⚠️ The card's "by omission, not by decision" reading is *stronger* than it reads

The card observed that `sys_file` declares no ADR-0103 `managedBy` bucket while seven sibling platform objects do. Re-derived during implementation, that is true — but the siblings do **not** all declare the same thing, and the distribution is the interesting part:

| object | declares |
|---|---|
| `sys-attachment.object.ts:34` | **`managedBy: 'platform'` — outright** |
| `sys-email:27`, `sys-job-run:24` | `append-only` |
| `sys-email-template:25` | `config` |
| `sys-job-queue:36`, `sys-job:24`, `sys-import-job:28` | `engine-owned` |

So `sys_file`'s **nearest sibling deliberately names the very bucket `sys_file` lands in by default**. The contrast is not "everyone else locked down and `sys_file` was forgotten" — it is "one sibling chose `platform` explicitly, and `sys_file` arrived there without anyone choosing". That sharpens the card's reading rather than softening it, and whoever rules the posture question will want it: the question is not "should `sys_file` be like its siblings" but "was `platform` ever decided for it, given the sibling that *did* decide it said so in writing".

### 2. The mechanism transferred verbatim, and the ablation controlled it

The booted fixture emitted **exactly** the denial line the card quoted — `operation 'update' on object 'sys_file' is not permitted for positions [everyone]` — so the object-level-RBAC reading is confirmed on a fresh fixture, not inherited from the original measurement.

The structural corroboration (the literal `sys_file` appears nowhere in `plugin-security/src`, so the baseline cannot be naming a grant for it) is a **zero-hit**, and zero-hits need a control before they count. Here the ablation *is* that control, in the strongest available form: injecting the missing grant into the baseline flipped the answer, which is direct evidence that the baseline's silence — and nothing else — was producing the refusal.

Ablation quality worth noting: the mutation was confirmed on disk by anchored greps **in both directions** (the injected marker present, the anchor still unique) plus a changed `git hash-object`, **and** in the built artifact the suite actually consumes — this suite resolves that package from `dist`, so an unrebuilt ablation would have stayed green and certified a vacuous pin. Predicted 4 refusal cases red / contrast control green; measured exactly that. Restore was byte-identical back to the recorded base hash, rebuilt, re-verified to a real green. The mutation script carried `trap restore EXIT INT TERM`, so an interrupted run could cost a reading but never leave the tree mutated.

⇒ **Not a tautology. Every refusal case was demonstrated capable of failing.**

### 3. The second-posture observation reproduced, without reproducing the harness

Under the ablation the seeded row's ownership held on **both** axes the platform tracks, and the ownership-floor RLS still refused neither non-admin persona. That independently confirms the card's second-posture observation — the one about ownership not being what holds this line — **as a property, without restating the withheld measurement**. Disclosure discipline intact.

### Status

CI on `fb0c37d6`: **33 checks, zero failures**, all six `Test Core` shards and the aggregator green; still running are the three Dogfood gates, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and three Type Check lanes. ⛔ Not flipped — green is read by job name when the run finishes. `Type Check · debt ledger` remains the job that discharges the declared local narrowing.

### Operational note, not a repo defect

The shared verify lock was heavily contended this round — two full 540s queue timeouts before the ablation got a slot. The dev spent those intervals on lock-free work rather than idling, which is the right handling, but it is worth knowing that ablation-heavy cards now pay a real queueing cost when several seats are active.

The question is not "should `sys_file` match its siblings" but "was `platform` ever decided for it".
- The pin is **compatible with every outcome** of that question by construction. If the posture tightens, the refusal stays a refusal. If it never does, this file is what reddens when the absence stops holding.

⛔ Still not decided here, and still a maintainer floor: whether `sys_file` should be engine-owned or these columns readonly / system-managed. Removing an affordance from app authors is not a call this seat makes.
